problems.form_value: other (measure_detail: 'Coded other: it measures carry-over from one's own earlier ideas, not the codebook's count of categories.')
problems.source_says: The paper names and operationalizes this measure as creative flexibility. It scores how far a participant's test-round ideas are from the exposure-round ideas, so it is variety among one person's own ideas, which codebook Section 6 codes flexibility. The form's reason for 'other' (not a count of categories) applies equally to S1-O5 and S1-O6, and the form codes those flexibility. The paper also calls the measure p-creativity (ideas novel to the individual), so novelty is the only other candidate. The paper implies, but does not state, that the Exposure set holds the participant's own ideas ('participant creative flexibility' in the Figure 4 caption).
problems.quote: In the framework of our experiment, we operationalize flexibility by checking how similar the ideas generated in the Test round are to the ideas generated in the Exposure rounds.
problems.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.3, 'Creative flexibility' bullet; PDF p. 3, Section 2.1 (P-creativity); PDF p. 7, Figure 4 caption; codebook Section 6 (Construct)

problems.form_value: participant (measure_detail: 'Aggregation to the participant is not described.')
problems.source_says: The paper defines the score for each test-round idea and never says it averages the score per participant. It reports the Experiment 1 results as 'the analysis of 9,457 ideas'. The only hint of a participant unit is the Figure 4 caption ('participant creative flexibility'). Section 3.2.3 calls the plotted value 'the average creative flexibility across conditions'. The text does not support 'participant', and 'output' fits the definition at least as well. The form codes S1-O1, whose score is also defined per idea, as output.
problems.quote: We measure this by finding the maximum cosine similarity between the embedding of an idea in the Test set and all the ideas in the Exposure set.
problems.locator: PDF p. 6, Sections 3.1.3 and 3.2 (9,457 ideas); PDF p. 7, Figure 4 caption; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 3.2.3

problems.form_value: participant (measure_detail of both admits the paper does not say whether the test pools rounds or averages them per person)
problems.source_says: The paper defines both measures per round. Fluency counts ideas 'in a given round', and the exposure result for individual diversity is stated 'within each round'. The exposure phase has three rounds per person. Neither the paper nor preregistration #189,206 (item 5) says whether the Kruskal-Wallis tests pool participant-rounds (three observations per person) or use one mean per person. 'participant' is therefore an assumption, not the unit of the paper's own analysis. The codebook has no participant-round code, so the unit field should carry the ambiguity, not only measure_detail.
problems.quote: We measure fluency by counting the number of ideas the participant generated in a given round.
problems.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.3; PDF p. 7, Section 3.2.2; PDF p. 8, Section 3.2.4 ('within each round'); PDF p. 4, Figure 2 ('3 Exposure Rounds'); AsPredicted #189,206 item 5

problems.form_value: automated_score (S2-O1 measure_detail: 'automated_score stands in for answer-key scoring (no code fits exactly)')
problems.source_says: Codebook Section 6 defines automated_score as a scoring model for creativity: semantic-distance scoring of divergent-thinking tests, or a language model used as judge. The paper describes no scoring model. It says only that each RAT problem has one correct answer and that the metric is accuracy. Preregistration #189,207 (item 3) counts correct answers. Answer-key accuracy fits no codebook measure, so the coded value has no support in the text or the codebook. It needs a codebook decision (a new code or a stated convention), not a placeholder.
problems.quote: Because a given RAT problem has a singular correct answer, we were able to define the metric for convergent thinking skills as accuracy on the RAT problems.
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 4.1; codebook Section 6 (Measure); AsPredicted #189,207 item 3

problems.source_says: The paper runs no test on exposure-round accuracy, so there is no analysis whose observation the unit can name. The only source is Figure 9, and its caption calls the plotted values 'participant accuracy'. 'output' is carried over from S2-O1, where the ANCOVA error df of 1256 supports one row per answer. No text supports it for S2-O2.
problems.quote: Figure 9: Plot of participant accuracy on the Remote Associates Task, segmented by exposure and test phase across all experimental conditions.
problems.locator: PDF p. 11, Figure 9 caption and Section 4.2.1

problems.source_says: Low severity. Codebook Section 6 defines set as one condition's whole pool of outputs. In this paper each observation is one Monte Carlo draw of 7 ideas, sampled across participants by condition, item, and phase, over 150 runs, and the Figure 5b values come from those draws. 'set' is the nearest code, and measure_detail describes the draws. Still, a resampled 7-idea subset is not what the codebook's definition covers, and the codebook has no code for it.
problems.quote: To achieve this, we performed 150 Monte Carlo runs, where we sampled 7 ideas per round, simulating group contribution dynamics.
problems.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.1.3 (group-level diversity bullet); PDF p. 8, Section 3.2.4; PDF p. 7, Figure 5 caption; codebook Section 6 (Unit)

RAT accuracy is convergent.

confirmed.statement: These units are supported. S1-O3 and S1-O5 are participant, because the test round gives each person one object. summary: Every c082 outcome is scored on participants' ideas or answers by a computed measure, the question codes follow the codebook rule, and all printed statistics and figure statements match the PDF, so criterion 3 holds. The coding is refuted on details: S1-O9 fits flexibility under the codebook's within-person rule and its participant unit is unsupported, the units of S1-O4, S1-O6, and S2-O2 are assumptions, automated_score does not fit answer-key RAT accuracy, and 'set' only approximates the 7-idea Monte Carlo draws.
